explanation: The L90M substitution introduces a more polar, sulfur-containing thiolether group that displaces the purely hydrophobic branched aliphatic side chain of leucine, reducing favorable van der Waals contacts within saquinavir's binding pocket at this C-terminal dimer interface. The modest loss of hydrophobic character (-1.9 kcal/mol equivalent) destabilizes the interaction without creating steric strain, as the similar volumes permit accommodation without obvious clashes. This selective weakening of nonpolar interactions in a hydrophobic subpocket region suggests that saquinavir's binding relies on precisely optimized hydrophobic complementarity at position 90, which the more polar methionine fails to adequately satisfy.
